title: GRADS: Graph-Regulated Agentic Data Synthesis with Controllable Difficulty
abstract: arXiv:2610.21167v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Deep research agents are increasingly deployed to retrieve precise information from large corpora, yet multi-hop, long-horizon tasks remain challenging. Synthetic data generation has emerged as a scalable solution, with existing pipelines typically expanding seed tasks to increase their apparent depth and breadth. However, this expansion does not reliably translate into necessary reasoning: newly introduced evidence may be only weakly coupled to the answer, creating a mismatch between intended and empirical difficulty. To address this problem, we introduce GRADS, a graph-guided agentic data synthesis framework with explicit difficulty control. GRADS runs a closed loop of seed selection, evidence expansion, question--answer construction, and verification while maintaining a graph of the evidence and inference dependencies required to derive each answer. translated_title: GRADS：具有可控难度的图调控智能体数据合成方法
translated_abstract: 深度研究智能体日益被部署用于从大规模语料库中检索精确信息，然而多跳、长程任务仍然充满挑战。合成数据生成已成为一种可扩展的解决方案，现有的流水线通常通过扩展种子任务来增加其表观的深度和广度。然而，这种扩展并不能可靠地转化为必要的推理能力：新引入的证据可能仅与答案弱耦合，从而造成预期难度与实际难度之间的不匹配。为了解决这一问题，我们提出了GRADS，一个具有显式难度控制的图引导智能体数据合成框架。GRADS运行一个闭环流程，包括种子选择、证据扩展、问答构建和验证，同时维护一个记录推导每个答案所需证据和推理依赖关系的图结构。在每一步中，它基于相关子图来约束生成过程，保持不可或缺的
tldr: GRADS提出了一种基于图结构的闭环智能体数据合成框架，通过维护证据与推理依赖图来显式控制合成数据的难度，解决了多跳长程推理任务中预期难度与实际难度不匹配的问题。
en_tdlr: GRADS introduces a closed-loop graph-guided agentic data synthesis framework that maintains evidence and inference dependency graphs to explicitly control the difficulty of synthetic data, addressing the mismatch between intended and empirical difficulty in multi-hop long-horizon reasoning tasks.
